hints.content: **Reflective (or line) symmetry** means that we can reflect a figure across a line, and the figure will remain unchanged.

##Reflection over $y=\dfrac{3}{5}x$

Under this transformation, some points on the parallelogram map to another point which is no longer on the parallelogram. The parallelogram is *not symmetric* over this line.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A parallelogram mapped onto a coordinate plane. The x- y-coordinate plane scales by ones. The center of the parallelogram is at the origin. The parallelogram has a point at negative seven, negative one, a point at negative three, negative five, a point at three, five, and a point at seven, one. The equation y equals three over five X is graphed on the coordinate plane. Dotted lines show the locations of the points after the parallelogram is reflected over the graphed line. The points of the image are not mapped on the current pre-image.

hints.content:
Neither symmetry applies to the parallelogram.

Symmetry | Applies to the figure?
:- | :-:
Reflective symmetry over the line $y=\dfrac{3}{5}x$ | No
Reflective symmetry over the line $y=\dfrac{5}{3}x$ | No
